messages.content: I need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu

function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.reasoning:
We have two names: parath and bhanu. We want both pending and active mandates for each? Or we want all pending AND active mandates across those users combined? Likely they want all pending or active mandates for those specific users.

The tool requires separate calls per user. So call user_mandates twice: once for parath, then for bhanu. For each, specify status as either "active" or "pending"? But if we want both statuses, maybe do two calls per user? However the question says "all pending and active mandates". That could mean get all mandates where status is either pending or active (i.e., not inactive). There's no direct filter for multiple statuses; but can request only one at a time. Could combine results after fetching separately.

Thus plan:

1) Call user_mandates(name="parath") -> returns active mandates by default. Then also call user_mandates(name="parath", status="pending").

2) Similarly for bhanu.

Alternatively, if the system supports specifying status optional param default active, so calling without status gives active. To include pending too, we might need second call.

So total four calls.

Let's proceed accordingly. We'll produce JSON output from each call. Use the function calls.
